faqs.question: Does "propose day quotes for love" mean quotes for a girlfriend?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. In Indian English "your love" is a form of address rather than a recipient label, so the same phrase is typed by people writing to a girlfriend, a boyfriend, a husband, a wife and someone they are not yet anything to. That is why the lines here are grouped by what you are allowed to call the person instead of by gender.

faqs.question: Is it safe to call someone "my love" if we are not dating yet?
faqs.answer: Usually not. "My love" reads as intimate only when the phrase is already in ordinary use between you; used cold, it answers a question that has not been asked. Use their first name and nothing else until the word has been earned.

faqs.question: What date is Propose Day in 2027?
faqs.answer: Monday 8 February 2027. It is the second day of Valentine week, after Rose Day on Sunday 7 February, and the week runs eight dated days to Valentine's Day on Sunday 14 February.

faqs.question: Can I send my wife the same line I would send a girlfriend?
faqs.answer: The line will work, but the address term inside it will not. A spouse already has a kinship word attached — wife, husband — and a line that avoids it reads as though you are starting over rather than asking again.

faqs.question: Should I write the line in English or in my mother tongue?
faqs.answer: Write the endearment in whichever language you actually use with that person. Research on terms of endearment across varieties shows the same category carrying different weight in different languages, so a borrowed word from a language neither of you speaks at home reads as costume.

faqs.question: How long should a Propose Day message be?
faqs.answer: One or two sentences. Propose Day 2027 falls on a working Monday, so most of these are read between meetings on a phone — 48.4% of SubhSandesh page views platform-wide are on a phone, across all 20 page types.

faqs.question: Is it strange to propose again to someone I already married?
faqs.answer: No, as long as it is sincere. A second ask works when it is offered as a real question rather than a joke; the kinship word you already use is the right address term for it.

faqs.question: What should I send if they said no last year?
faqs.answer: Send something with no address term in it at all. A line that reopens the question puts them back in the position of refusing you, so say what you understood instead and leave the question closed.

faqs.question: Do I have to credit a quote I copy from a website?
faqs.answer: You do not need to credit an unattributed line, but you must not invent an attribution. Appending a famous name to a line you found on a listicle is the one mistake that is worse than sending nothing.

faqs.question: Is "jaan" too informal for a proposal?
faqs.answer: Only if it is not already your word for them. Endearments work as markers of closeness and informality, so "jaan" in a proposal reads as warm from someone who uses it daily and as performance from someone who does not.

faqs.question: Should the line go in a message or on a page?
faqs.answer: A message suits a single sentence; a page suits a line you want them to keep. If you are asking someone to marry you, the proposal scrapbook is the better container, and 38.7% of SubhSandesh creators password-protect a page before sharing it, platform-wide.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Propose Day Quotes for Love, Sorted by What You Call Them

"Propose day quotes for love" is not a recipient query, which is why most lists answer it badly. In Indian English "your love" covers a girlfriend, a boyfriend, a husband, a wife and someone who is not yet anything to you, so the first decision is not which line to copy but which word it is allowed to use for them. This page sorts by that word: 16 original lines in six groups, each naming who may send it and where it goes wrong, grounded in SubhSandesh's platform-wide numbers — 5,061 personalised pages built since 12 March 2026 across 20 page types, of which the "I love you" page is 1,173 pages, 23.2% of everything created — and dated correctly to Monday 8 February 2027.

## What "for love" actually means in this search

"For love" is a form of address, not a relationship label: it is the Indian-English habit of calling a partner "my love" and using that phrase where other varieties would name the person's role. It works like "my better half" or "my jaan" — the endearment stands in for the noun, which is how 1 search phrase ends up serving 5 different relationships.

That matters because the word leaks the relationship. A line built on "my love" reads as intimate when the phrase is already in use and presumptuous when it is not, and someone still deciding whether to ask a person out cannot borrow a spouse's line.

## Why the address term decides the line, not the other way round

Endearments are a studied sub-category of address forms. Analysing 312 interactions with 199 endearment terms — 87 English, 112 Arabic — from 45 hours of American and Syrian television drama, [Khalil and Larina's 2022 study in the *RUDN Journal of Language Studies, Semiotics and Semantics*](https://journals.rudn.ru/semiotics-semantics/article/view/30699) found them marking informality, closeness and emotive politeness, with the Syrian Arabic set more variable and more conventional, able to carry respect and deference too. Endearments do not port: a word that signals warmth in one variety signals deference in another.

Indian English is a contact variety with its own etiquette. [Rogovets's 2019 paper in *Polylinguality and Transcultural Practices*](https://journals.rudn.ru/polylinguality/article/view/21829) traces the formula "What is your good name?" and argues Indian English politeness patterns carry transfer from Hindi and other regional languages, because conventions exist here for which English has no equivalent. That is why "my love" is ordinary in Delhi and theatrical in London.

Endearments also drift: [Grząśko's 2015 study in *LingBaW*](https://czasopisma.kul.pl/index.php/LingBaW/article/view/5626) shows *honey*, *sugar* and *pumpkin* became endearments by metaphor from food and plants, while other words stopped being endearments altogether.

An address system is a structure, not a word list. A study of the Pubian dialect of Lampung, published in *Kervan* on 27 December 2019, [sorts its address terms into ten categories](https://www.ojs.unito.it/index.php/kervan/article/view/3609) — kinship by blood and by marriage, endearment, birth order and more — each with rules for use.

Multilingual settings draw on several pools at once: [Unuabonah's 2018 study in *Linguistik Online*](https://bop.unibe.ch/linguistik-online/article/view/4398) found address forms at a Nigerian university drawn from English, Yoruba, Nigerian Pidgin and other languages. India works the same way, which is why "my love", "jaan" and a bare first name are three registers open to one couple.

## 16 Propose Day quotes for your love, grouped by what you call them

Each group names who it fits, the address term, the lines and where it fails.

### 1. First name only, because there is no word for this yet

**Who it fits:** you are not together; Propose Day is the excuse.
**The address term:** their name, nothing else.
**The lines:**

> "There is no word for what we are yet. I would like to find one with you."

> "I am not asking you to be anything today. I am asking whether you would like a word for this."

**Where it goes wrong:** an endearment answers a question they were never asked.

### 2. "My love", when the phrase is already in use between you

**Who it fits:** a couple where the word is already ordinary.
**The address term:** "my love", used the way you already use it.
**The lines:**

> "You have been my love since before I said it out loud. Today I am saying it out loud."

> "I call you my love in my head about forty times a day. Consider this the first honest count."

> "'My love' stopped being a habit around March. Somewhere in there it became accurate."

**Where it goes wrong:** if you have never said it aloud, this is a strange debut.

### 3. Their full name, when an endearment would soften a serious ask

**Who it fits:** you are asking to marry, and you want it read as a decision.
**The address term:** the whole name, unshortened.
**The lines:**

> "No nickname, no build-up: I want the rest of it with you."

> "I am using your full name because I want you to know I am serious. Will you marry me?"

> "Everyone else shortens your name. I would like to keep saying all of it, for a long time."

**Where it goes wrong:** it reads cold if the question is only "will you go out with me".

### 4. A borrowed endearment, when English is not the language of the feeling

**Who it fits:** bilingual couples, where the English line is accurate and the mother-tongue one true.
**The address term:** jaan, sona, chellam, priya — whichever is yours.
**The lines:**

> "I can say this in English and it comes out polite. In Hindi it comes out true, so: jaan, will you?"

> "You are the only person I have called sona and meant it as a job description."

> "My English is better than my Tamil. My Tamil is better at this."

**Where it goes wrong:** an endearment from a language neither of you speaks at home is costume.

### 5. "My wife" or "my husband", asking the person you married

**Who it fits:** married or engaged couples, asking again on purpose.
**The address term:** the kinship word you already use.
**The lines:**

> "The word is already ours. I am asking again anyway, because nobody should be asked only once in a life."

> "Nobody proposes to the person they already married. I am going to."

**Where it goes wrong:** played as a joke it deflates. A second ask works only sincere.

### 6. No address term at all, after a no or after a fight

**Who it fits:** you asked and were turned down, or you are mid-repair.
**The address term:** none. You have not earned one back yet.
**The lines:**

> "I am not going to call you anything I have not earned back. So: will you talk to me on Monday?"

> "You said no once and you were allowed to. I am not asking again today — I am telling you I understood it."

> "I do not have a right to a nickname right now. I do have one thing to say, and this is it."

**Where it goes wrong:** a heart emoji and a rose photo. The restraint is the message.

## Which address term fits which reader

Six groups, the sender behind each, and the page that suits, with platform-wide shares.

| What you call them | Who is sending it | What the line must avoid | Template that fits (platform-wide share of 5,061 pages) |
|---|---|---|---|
| First name only | Not a couple yet | assuming a yes | "I love you" page — 1,173 created, 23.2% |
| "My love" | Together, endearment established | sounding like a caption | "I love you" page — most-viewed, 16,902 views, 30.1% |
| Full name | Asking to marry | softening the question | proposal scrapbook — one of 20 page types |
| Borrowed endearment | Bilingual couple | explaining the word | "I love you" page — 1,173 created, 23.2% |
| No address term | After a no or a fight | reopening the question | apology dashboard — 1,347 created, 26.6% |

The last column is the honest part: the most-created page is an apology, not a proposal.

## Propose Day 2027 falls on Monday 8 February

Rose Day opens Valentine week on Sunday 7 February 2027, Propose Day is the second day, Monday 8 February, and Valentine's Day closes it on Sunday 14 February — eight dated days, not seven. Unlike 2026, it is a working Monday.

That changes delivery more than wording. A line sent at 9.40 a.m. on a working Monday is read between meetings, which argues for one sentence, not four; 48.4% of SubhSandesh views platform-wide are on a phone (27,185 of 56,152).

If you are genuinely asking someone to marry you, a copied line is the wrong instrument and the [proposal scrapbook page](/proposal) is the right one: it walks your story to the question. If you are not proposing marriage — and most people typing this phrase are not — the honest alternative is the ["I love you" page](/love-gf), the second-most-created template at 1,173 pages, 23.2% of everything built, and most-viewed at 16,902 views, 30.1%. Start early: the median first-save-to-last-edit gap is 2.4 hours, sampled on the apology dashboard template, n=1,348.

## When a Propose Day quote is the wrong thing to send

If you already know who you are writing to, sorting by address term is work you do not need. Two siblings go deeper on one recipient each: [propose day quotes for a girlfriend](/blog/propose-day-quotes-for-girlfriend) sorts by situation, and [propose day quotes for a boyfriend](/blog/propose-day-quotes-for-boyfriend) sorts by how he receives them.

A quote is also wrong when they have signalled nothing back: a sent line demands a reply, and on a Monday it arrives in public. If the person is in the same room, say it out loud instead.

One limit on every number above: SubhSandesh holds no proposal-specific data, so each figure is platform-wide across 20 page types or sampled on a named template. 91.2% of started pages are published and shared (4,615 of 5,061) and 38.7% of creators password-protect the page first (1,961 of 5,061) — both platform-wide.

- Rogovets, "'What is Your Good Name?'", *Polylinguality and Transcultural Practices*, 2019 — [English abstract](https://journals.rudn.ru/polylinguality/article/view/21829)
- Grząśko, "On the semantic history of selected terms of endearment", *LingBaW*, 2015 — [article](https://czasopisma.kul.pl/index.php/LingBaW/article/view/5626)

auditReport.honestAssessment: This is a copy-text query with near-zero conversion — the searcher copies a line and closes the tab — so the page should be judged on impressions and on whether an answer engine lifts the address-term grouping, not on sign-ups. What it has that the ranking set does not is a resolution of the ambiguity in "for love": it is the only version here that treats the phrase as Indian-English address rather than assuming a girlfriend, sorts its lines by the word the sender is entitled to use, and grounds that split in cross-linguistic address-form research (312 interactions, 199 endearment terms) plus first-party platform-wide figures no competitor can publish. Against that: the SERP was measured once on a US-served search and the ranking pages were never fetched, so the differentiation claim rests on the page's own construction rather than on a measured comparison; the domain sits far below the gifting retailers and wishes aggregators that own this query, and Propose Day traffic is a February spike, so realistic expectation is a mid-page position in the 2027 cycle at the earliest.
